explanation: The plexus of Bonnet (hair follicle receptor network) is a mechanoreceptor formed by free nerve endings that wrap around hair follicles to detect hair movement.
Pacinian corpuscles and Ruffini endings are the deepest tactile receptors, located in the dermis and hypodermis for vibration and stretch detection.
Muscle spindles contain intrafusal fibers with gamma motor neuron innervation that adjusts sensitivity, unlike other receptors listed which are purely sensory.
Golgi tendon organs lack gamma motor innervation (unlike muscle spindles), are in series with muscle, and detect tension; both have capsules.
Substantia gelatinosa (Roland's substance) corresponds to Rexed lamina II of the posterior horn, specializing in pain and temperature modulation.
Clarke's nucleus (dorsocentral nucleus) is located in Rexed lamina VII at T1-L2 levels, serving as the origin of the dorsal spinocerebellar tract.
Gamma motor neurons are located in Rexed lamina IX of the anterior horn, innervating intrafusal muscle fibers within muscle spindles.
Bilateral loss of vibration and position sense with preserved pain/temperature indicates gracile tract lesion, as it carries proprioception and vibration from the legs.
The RAS receives sensory input from proprioceptors and various sensory modalities to maintain cortical arousal and alertness.
Delta waves (0.5-2 Hz, high amplitude) are the hallmark of deep slow-wave sleep in adults, replacing alpha rhythms.
Operant (instrumental) conditioning is associative learning where behavior is modified by its consequences (reward or punishment).
The lateral hypothalamus is the feeding (hunger) center; stimulation produces hunger and eating behavior, while destruction causes anorexia.
Semantic memory stores general facts, concepts, and knowledge independent of personal experience (declarative/explicit memory).
The representational (non-dominant) hemisphere in most people lies in the right hemisphere and is specialized for spatial and holistic processing.
GABA-A receptors are ligand-gated chloride channels; chloride influx hyperpolarizes the neuron, causing inhibition.
The periaqueductal grey (PAG) in the midbrain contains endogenous opioid neurons that activate descending pain inhibition pathways.
A-delta fibers (myelinated, fast-conducting) transmit first/quick pain, while C fibers (unmyelinated) transmit slow, throbbing second pain.
Opioid receptor stimulation activates descending pain inhibition pathways, reducing pain transmission at the spinal cord level.
Mechanoreceptors detect the light touch sensation tested by cotton wool; they include Meissner corpuscles and Merkel discs.
Weber's two-point compass test assesses tactile discrimination ability, testing the spatial resolution of Meissner and Merkel receptors.
Phenytoin is associated with fetal hydantoin syndrome causing cleft lip/palate, digital hypoplasia, and growth retardation.
Apomorphine (subcutaneous dopamine agonist) is used as rescue therapy for sudden off-periods in advanced Parkinson's disease.
Propranolol (beta-blocker) is first-line treatment for antipsychotic-induced akathisia, likely by blocking beta-2 receptors in the locus coeruleus.
Lithium has delayed onset (weeks), narrow therapeutic index (0.6-1.2 mEq/L), and requires regular serum level monitoring.
Clozapine and carbamazepine both cause agranulocytosis; their combination dramatically increases this risk and is contraindicated.
Topiramate is used for migraine prophylaxis and causes weight loss and renal calcium phosphate stones (carbonic anhydrase inhibition).
Venlafaxine (SNRI) and duloxetine are antidepressants approved for diabetic neuropathy and other chronic pain conditions.
Ester local anesthetics are MORE liable to cause allergic reactions due to para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) metabolite, not less.
Phenobarbital is justified long-term only for certain epilepsies (generalized tonic-clonic, partial seizures) due to its side effect profile.
Carbidopa inhibits peripheral aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase, preventing peripheral levodopa conversion and increasing CNS availability.
Naltrexone (opioid antagonist) is used in alcohol dependence treatment by blocking opioid receptors involved in the rewarding effects of alcohol.
MAC (minimum alveolar concentration) defines potency as the alveolar concentration that prevents movement in 50% of patients to a surgical stimulus.
Acyclovir (guanine analog) is the treatment of choice for HSV encephalitis in neonates, reducing mortality when given early.
Cryptococcus neoformans produces melanin via phenol oxidase, which protects against oxidative stress and is a major virulence factor.
Tetanus vaccine contains inactivated tetanus toxin (toxoid) that stimulates antibody production without causing disease.
